verification.method: scripts/verify/migration-113.py reads the original World Bank zips (data/raw/wdi/), not the site's generated data; check-wdi.mjs compares all generated WDI values with the original files; then the text was read by hand
verification.what: every ranking row (216 countries and areas, order and value), the number-of-migrants and 1990 columns, the CSV, every figure in the text, FAQ, title, description and JSON-LD; claims: Qatar 76.7% and UAE 74.0% (about three in four), Qatar's peak of 86.1% in 2015, Kuwait 7th, 18 places above half and 40 below 1%, world 3.7%, high-income 14.7%, low and middle income 1.4%, South Asia 0.5%, biggest rises since 2000 in Aruba and Malta, Spain 2.1% / 4.9% / 18.5%, Chile and Colombia, lowest China, Madagascar, Myanmar, Philippines and Cuba, Bangladesh 1.7% (159th) more than doubled from 0.8%; definitions and caveats from the indicator notes
verification.against: World Bank WDI bulk files and indicator metadata (update 11 November 2026, CC BY 4.0; UN DESA International Migrant Stock)
verification.result: Before publishing, an unverifiable 'among larger countries' phrase about Spain was removed and Saint Martin's 0.0% (a doubtful value) is not quoted in the text. All automated comparisons matched

changelog.note: First version: UN DESA International Migrant Stock via World Bank WDI, 2024.
